title: DATRAS Frequently Asked Questions
text:
Overview of DATRAS

What is DATRAS?
DATRAS is an online database of trawl surveys hosted by ICES. It stores data from internationally coordinated fish trawl surveys in ICES area 27 in a standardised format and provides a data quality check upon upload. The DATRAS portal offers online services for uploading and downloading survey data.


What can DATRAS data be used for?
DATRAS is used by ICES expert groups, national institutes, and researchers for verifying, storing, and obtaining fisheries-independent sampling data. The data can be used in stock assessments, biodiversity studies, and other fisheries-related projects. All data products are accessible under ICES Data Policy.


What is the timespan of DATRAS data?
Each survey has its own timeline. The oldest records are from 1965 (NS-IBTS). A full overview of survey coverage, including first and last year and valid haul counts, is given in the D2.2 surveys table.


Which surveys are available via DATRAS?
DATRAS currently holds data from 29 surveys covering the Northeast Atlantic (as of 2026). The 2014 version of this document listed 15 surveys; the inventory has grown substantially. See the D2.2 surveys table for the full current list. Surveys include NS-IBTS, BITS, BTS, EVHOE, IE-IGFS, NIGFS, FR-CGFS, SP-NORTH, SP-PORC, SP-ARSA, PT-IBTS, and many others.


Which data products can I get from DATRAS?
All uploaded survey data can be downloaded as raw exchange data (HH, HL, CA record types). Some surveys also offer standard derived data products computed by the ICES expert groups:



Product
Description




CPUEL
CPUE-by-length per haul


CPUEA
CPUE-by-age per haul


IDX
Survey abundance indices


CW
Catch weight by species


FL
Survey-specific flex file (additional fields)


LT
Marine litter assessment



From April 2012, all data products include a DateofCalculation field for tracking changes.


How do I acknowledge use of DATRAS data?
Follow the ICES Data Policy. Example citations:

ICES Database of Trawl Surveys (DATRAS). ICES, Copenhagen. https://datras.ices.dk


ICES DATRAS, Extraction [DATE]. [Survey name] data [year range]. ICES, Copenhagen. https://datras.ices.dk



What are the data use restrictions?
DATRAS data are available under the ICES open access data policy (adopted 2006, updated 2012). Aggregated data and raw data are freely available under these conditions.

title: DATRAS Frequently Asked Questions
text:
For Data Users

Downloading data

How do I access trawl survey data?
Survey data and derived products can be downloaded from the DATRAS download page. Note that the web portal limits downloads to 1 million records. For larger datasets, split the download into smaller parts (e.g. by year or quarter) or use the ICES web services / {obus} parquet access (dr_con()) for efficient bulk access without record limits.


Why are not all data products available for all surveys?
DATRAS data products are developed and verified in cooperation with the relevant ICES Expert Groups. This is a time-consuming process, and newer surveys may not yet have derived products. Currently CPUEL is available for 8 of the 29 surveys (BITS, EVHOE, IE-IGFS, NS-IBTS, ROCKALL, SCOROC, SCOWCGFS, SWC-IBTS).


What are “Standard species”?
Standard species are the target species of a given survey. While all surveys aim to record all species caught, each survey has one or more target species for which detailed biological data (sex, maturity, age, individual weight) are collected. Age-based data products (CPUEA, IDX) are therefore available only for standard species. Refer to the relevant survey manual for the standard species list.



Understanding the data format

How do I understand the DATRAS exchange file format?
Exchange data are the raw survey data as submitted by national institutes. Each file contains three record types:







Record
Content




HH
Haul Header — one row per haul; gear, position, timing, validity


HL
Haul-level Length — catch by length class per species per haul


CA
Catch-at-age — individual biological measurements



The three record types share a common set of haul identification fields and are linked by the composite haul key .id (constructed from Survey, Year, Quarter, Country, Platform (Ship), Gear, StationName (StNo), HaulNumber (HaulNo)). In the raw CSV submission format, these correspond to the first 11 fields common to all record types.


What does “−9” stand for?
−9 is the DATRAS sentinel value for a missing or inapplicable field. It is not a real measurement. In the IMBUS standardised product ({obus}, parquet files) all −9 values are replaced with proper NA.


What are haul duration, vessel speed, and trawl parameters?
Standard values for HaulDuration (HaulDur), vessel speed, and gear parameters are defined in the survey manuals. Actual values as recorded during the haul are reported in the HH record fields HaulDuration (HaulDur), GroundSpeed, Distance, DoorSpread, WingSpread, and WarpLength.


Are catch figures adjusted for hauling time?
This depends on DataType in the HH record. See DataType and HL field interpretation for details.


Are all species reported in DATRAS?
Surveys intend to record all species caught, but it is the responsibility of the national data submitter whether all species are reported. The fields SpeciesValidity (SpecVal) in HL (field 26 in the raw HH record) and SpeciesCategory (CatIdentifier) (field 27) provide further context. Some surveys report a limited species list; refer to the survey manual.
In CA records, mainly standard survey species are reported.


What is SpeciesValidity (SpecVal)?
SpeciesValidity in HL records specifies how the species was handled:







Value
Meaning




1
Full record: lengths, numbers, weights — use in standard products


0
Invalid


4
Total number only; no lengths measured


5
Presence/absence only


6
Weight only


7
Numbers and weights; no lengths


10
Lengths and numbers; no weights



Only SpeciesValidity == "1" records are used in DATRAS-derived data products. Records with other values may still be of value for biodiversity or non-standard analyses.
SpeciesValidity is also linked to haul validity: if the haul was invalid or used for calibration, SpeciesValidity will reflect this.


What species reference system is used?
Species codes currently used for submissions are WoRMS AphiaIDs (SpeciesCodeType (SpecCodeType) = "W"). In historical submissions ITIS TSN ("T") and NODC ("N") codes were used. For cross-era analysis, all submitted codes are mapped to validated WoRMS AphiaIDs in the field ValidAphiaID (Valid_Aphia / Valid_WoRMS) in HL and CA records. Always use ValidAphiaID as the join key for species — never the raw SpeciesCode (SpecCode).
In derived data products (CPUEL, CPUEA, IDX), species are identified by valid Latin names or AphiaIDs.


Where can I find species names for codes in the file?
Species names can be matched to codes via the DATRAS Species Query Tool or directly via the WoRMS database.
If work in R you can also try this:
icesVocab::findAphia(c("cod", "haddock", "saithe"))
icesVocab::findAphia("Gadus morhuha", latin = TRUE)


Where can I find information about species maximum length?
Per-survey maximum length classes (mm) are listed on the DATRAS reporting format page (DATSU). Note that this list is static and was last updated in January 2011.


What area codes are used in DATRAS?
Area information appears in several places:

Haul positions: ShootLatitude/ShootLongitude and HaulLatitude/HaulLongitude in HH, reported as decimal degrees.
Statistical rectangle: StatisticalRectangle (StatRec) in HH, based on shooting position (unless the majority of the haul was in the adjacent rectangle).
Depth strata: DepthStratum (Stratum) in HH, for surveys with depth-stratified sampling.
Age-sampling areas: AreaCode and AreaType in CA, indicating whether the age sample is haul-level (AreaType == "H") or area-pooled. Always check AreaType before joining CA records to HH.

ICES statistical rectangles are described at the ICES maps page.


Do DATRAS data pass any quality validation?
Yes. Before upload, all files pass the DATSU screening utility, which applies logical, value, and vocabulary checks. Critical errors must be corrected before the file can be uploaded; warnings are non-critical. Weight-length outlier graphs are also provided as an additional screening tool.
Every year, responsible expert groups review their data and report irrelevancies to the DATRAS team. If you find erroneous data, contact DATRAS administration (DATRASAdministration@ices.dk).



CPUE and derived products

What is CPUE in DATRAS?
CPUE (catch per unit effort) in DATRAS is the catch in numbers of individuals of the same species, adjusted to one hour of hauling.


If I compare CPUE per length values to the exchange file, they don’t match. Why?
Exchange files contain data as submitted, potentially in DataType R (raw), S (sub-sampled), or C (catch per unit effort). CPUE data products display numbers raised to one hour of hauling. To compare, you must apply the appropriate raising formula to the exchange data. See DataType and HL field interpretation for the correct formula per DataType.


What do zeroes mean in a CPUE product?
A CPUE value of zero means the species was absent from that haul but was caught by at least one vessel in the same survey/year/quarter. Zero records are automatically added to all hauls where the species was absent. Explicit zero rows are required for unbiased abundance indices.
A species may also have a zero if the data submitter observed but did not record biological data. Refer to the exchange file for details.


A species is missing from CPUE for some years/quarters. Why?
Records for a species in a CPUE product appear only if at least one submitter observed and reported it in that year/quarter. If no submitter reported the species in a given year/quarter, no records (including zeroes) will be present in the product.


Why are age records limited to age_6 or age_10 in age-based products?
Age-based products are designed according to requirements from the responsible ICES Expert Group. Groups specify a plus group age, above which all fish are aggregated (e.g. NS-IBTS uses plus group age 6: all fish aged 6+ are recorded as age 6).


What is country code DUM (DUMMY)?
Country code DUM was used for reporting historical age data from Danish commercial vessels with platform codes DCA and HOL in 1983–1995.


Where are BITS data before 1991?
BITS started in the early 1980s but was not standardised until 1991. The responsible expert group (WGBIFS) decided that only data from 1991 onward should be available via DATRAS. Contact WGBIFS for access to earlier data.


Where do I find survey abundance indices?
DATRAS provides CPUE-by-length and CPUE-by-age products for standard species. These are accessible via dr_get("IDX", ...) in {obus}. Note that no weight-based products are currently available from DATRAS.


Is there a tool to convert age to weight?
Not directly. You can use the CA records (including individual weight measurements where available) to construct your own age–weight relationship.


Can I see when data were last corrected?
The DATRAS Submission Status page shows when the last cruise submission was made. The current DATRAS version does not show what was changed in a re-submission.

title: DATRAS Frequently Asked Questions
text:
For Data Submitters

General

What is the deadline for my submission?
Submission deadlines are listed on the DATRAS home page. Contact DATRAS administration if you are unsure.


How should my data file be formatted?
DATRAS accepts CSV files (comma-separated, decimal point ., no blank fields — use −9 for missing values, no headers). One file should contain all record types (HH, HL, CA) for the same year, quarter, country, vessel, and gear. All fields from the reporting format must be present.


Which units and codes should be used?
Field descriptions, units, and valid codes are in the DATRAS Reporting Format documentation and in the ICES Vocabulary Server (https://vocab.ices.dk/). Within {obus}, valid codes are also available via dr_lookup_vocabulary.


How do I get access to the DATRAS upload page?
Write to DATRAS administration and the Chair of the associated ICES Expert Group with your submitter details and access request.



Submission process

How do I submit my file?
Direct upload is available for most surveys from the DATRAS uploading page. Follow the instructions in “How to upload data into DATRAS” (available in the Documents section).


What quality control does my file pass?
Files pass the DATSU screening utility before upload:

Critical errors must be corrected; the file cannot be uploaded until they are resolved.
Warnings are non-critical; the submitter decides whether to correct them.
Information messages do not affect uploading.

Screening results are displayed on the DATRAS page and sent to the submitter’s email. If a screening message is unclear, click the question mark in the screening results table for more detail. If still unclear, contact DATRAS administration with your file and a screenshot.


What is error grouping in DATSU?
When the same error occurs many times, DATSU groups them into a single entry with a count. The submitter can expand the group to see individual occurrences. This avoids scrolling through thousands of identical messages.


I get “the survey selected does not include the country present in the file”. What is wrong?
Check:

The country code matches the vocabulary at https://vocab.ices.dk/?ref=4.
Numbers use a decimal point (.), not a decimal comma.
Your account has upload rights for this survey. Contact DATRAS administration if not.



I cannot find my uploaded data on the download page.
Check the DATRAS Submission Status page. If your submission is listed there with the correct upload time, the upload was successful. Updates to the download page may take a few days due to manual quality-control processing. If the data are needed urgently, contact DATRAS administration.


Can I make a partial re-submission by haul or record type?
No. DATRAS requires a complete re-submission per year, quarter, country, vessel, and gear.


What happens to existing data when I re-submit?
Existing data are overwritten when the data warehouse is updated. Always keep a copy of previous submissions. Note: if you re-submit with different key values (year, quarter, country, vessel, gear), the old data will not be overwritten — contact DATRAS administration to remove duplicates.


Can I document what was changed in a re-submission?
Yes — use the remarks box at the final upload step. You are also welcome to email DATRAS administration describing the corrections made.



Technical issues for data submitters

DataType and HL field interpretation
DataType is set at the haul level (HH record) and governs how HL fields must be interpreted. It is the most common source of silent errors when working with exchange data.








DataType
Description
CPUE formula




R
Raw; catch sorted, some species may be sub-sampled. SubsamplingFactor ≥ 1
n_haul = Σ(NumberAtLength × SubsamplingFactor)


S
Bulk unsorted catch sub-sampled before sorting. SubsamplingFactor > 1
Same as R


P
Size-stratified subsampling — different SubsamplingFactor per size grade. Do not sum TotalNumber across strata.
Same row-level formula as R, applied per stratum


C
Catch pre-raised to 1 hour of hauling. SubsamplingFactor = 1
n_hour = NumberAtLength; n_haul = NumberAtLength × HaulDuration / 60



The {obus} function dr_HL_standardised() applies the correct formula for all DataTypes automatically. For full field-by-field specifications and empirical notes on DataType misuse in submissions, see DATRAS Technical Reference §DataType.


What is SpeciesCategory (CatIdentifier), and how do I use it?
SpeciesCategory (CatIdentifier) is the ID assigned to a size- or weight-based subsampling stratum for a given species and sex within a haul. It is used when a truly representative sub-sample cannot be selected from the whole catch — for example, when larger fish are sorted away and measured separately with a different sub-sampling factor.

Assign SpeciesCategory = 1 to the first stratum and SpeciesCategory = 2, 3, … to additional strata (up to 5 per species per haul).
If no size categorisation was applied, use SpeciesCategory = 1 throughout.
Reporting different sex categories for the same species does not require different SpeciesCategory values — keep SpeciesCategory = 1 and vary SpeciesSex (Sex) instead.

See the NS-IBTS survey manual (section “Length composition”) for worked examples.


How is Day/Night defined?
Daytime is defined as the period from 15 minutes before sunrise to 15 minutes after sunset, following NOAA’s solar calculations. The derived field DayNight in HH is populated by the ICES datacenter from the shooting position and time.


Which area/position should I report?

Coordinates: ShootLatitude/ShootLongitude and HaulLatitude/HaulLongitude in HH, as decimal degrees.
Statistical rectangle: StatisticalRectangle (StatRec) in HH, based on shooting position.
Depth strata: DepthStratum (Stratum) in HH, if sampling is depth-stratified.
CA area codes: AreaCode and AreaType in CA, specifying haul-level vs. area-pooled age sampling.



How do I submit area-based CA data without corresponding HL data?
CA records must always be related to a parent HL record. If age sampling was area-based, create a dummy HL record by duplicating fields 2–12 from the CA record and setting all other HL fields to −9.
Example CA record:
CA,1,SCO,SCO3,GOV,60,-9,P,S01,1,2010,W,126417,2,3,0,140,U,-9,-9,3,1,-9
Corresponding dummy HL record:
HL,1,SCO,SCO3,GOV,60,-9,P,S01,1,2010,W,126417,0,-9,-9,-9,-9,-9,-9,-9,-9,-9,-9


Species codes and SpeciesCodeType (SpecCodeType)
Current submissions use WoRMS AphiaIDs (SpeciesCodeType = "W"). Historical data used ITIS TSN ("T") and NODC ("N") codes. All codes are mapped to current WoRMS AphiaIDs in the field ValidAphiaID (Valid_Aphia / Valid_WoRMS). For all analysis, use ValidAphiaID as the species join key.

title: DATRAS Frequently Asked Questions
text:
IMBUS Additions
The questions below were not in the original ICES FAQ. They arose from exploratory analysis of the DATRAS exchange tables conducted as part of IMBUS WP2.

What do HL records with a missing LengthClass represent?






Note



[IMBUS] This question was not in the original ICES FAQ. It arose from IMBUS WP2 exploratory analysis of the DATRAS HL table.


In the HL exchange table, records where LengthClass is NA (encoded as −9 in raw CSV files) are catch-totals rows. They record aggregate catch information for a species within a haul but carry no individual length measurement. Every such row also has NumberAtLength = NA. They are distinct from length-frequency rows in both purpose and content.
Catch-totals rows typically carry one or more of:







Field
Content




TotalNumber
Total count of fish in the haul (raised; or per hour for DataType C)


SubsampledNumber
Number of fish actually handled or weighed


SpeciesCategoryWeight
Catch weight for the species/category


SubsamplingFactor
Raising factor (may be 1 if all fish were counted)



These rows arise in two situations:

Species measured by count or weight only — where SpeciesValidity ≠ 1 (e.g. 4 = total number only, 6 = weight only, 7 = numbers and weights but no lengths). In this case the catch-totals row is the only HL record for that species.
Companion summary rows — present alongside a full length-frequency series for the same species/haul (typically SpeciesValidity = 1). The catch-totals row then summarises what the length rows describe individually.

Key implication for analysis: always filter !is.na(LengthClass) (and !is.na(NumberAtLength)) before computing CPUE or length distributions. Catch-totals rows cannot be raised via sum(NumberAtLength × SubsamplingFactor) — they carry no NumberAtLength. The {obus} function dr_add_n_and_cpue() handles this automatically.
TotalNumber in catch-totals rows is useful as a cross-check against the raised sum from the length-frequency rows, but note that its scope (all-sex total vs. sex-specific) is not consistent across surveys; see the DATRAS data issues for a survey-by-survey reconciliation.

What is the difference between DataType “P” and “R”?
Short answer: DataType R (raw catch) is for hauls where the entire catch is sorted and some species are sub-sampled at a single rate. DataType P (pseudocategory) is for hauls where the catch is sorted into multiple size grades, each with its own sub-sampling rate.

Why the distinction exists:

DataType P explicitly signals that size-stratification is present, so downstream users understand that multiple SpeciesCategory rows per species per haul are expected, and each TotalNumber corresponds to a size stratum.
DataType R signals that there is one sub-sampling rate per species; users can be confident that summing by species will yield the haul total.

Recommended practice for users: - Always use the row-level formula: n_haul = Σ(NumberAtLength × SubsamplingFactor) per haul and species - The {obus} function dr_add_n_and_cpue() handles all DataTypes correctly


Why do we have more than one value for SpeciesValidity within the same tow (.id) for the same species?
SpeciesValidity is a record type field — it describes what kind of data is present for a species within a haul, not whether the haul is valid. The HL exchange format allows more than one record type for the same species and haul, and some surveys use this deliberately.
A typical scenario: a species was fully length-measured ("1", full record), but the crew also recorded a total count for a size group that was not individually measured ("4", total number only), or noted a presence/absence for bycatch ("5"). Both rows share the same .id × aphia group, so SpeciesValidity is not constant within that group.
This is intentional, not an error. BTS and Can-Mar are the main surveys that submit multiple record types for the same species and haul. Across all surveys, ~2,786 of ~2.6 million HL groups (0.1%) show this pattern. The most common co-occurrences are {1, 5} and {4, 7}.

This is the intended semantics of SpeciesValidity = "5" as defined in the DATRAS format.
Can-Mar exception. Can-Mar uses SpeciesValidity = "5" differently — on rows that carry actual LengthClass and NumberAtLength values. Across 535 Can-Mar groups with both "1" and "5" rows containing length data, 42% have entirely distinct length classes between the two record types (the "5" rows add lengths not in the "1" rows), 20% are full duplicates, and 38% partially overlap. Practical implication: if you aggregate over .id × aphia without also grouping on SpeciesValidity, rows from different record types will be silently mixed together. For most surveys (including BTS), filter to SpeciesValidity == "1" before aggregating to retain only the full length-frequency records. For Can-Mar, the appropriate treatment of SpeciesValidity = "5" rows with length data is currently unresolved.

title: Survey Abundance Indices — Calculation Procedures
text:
Extracted from ICES Data Centre DATRAS Procedure Documents: NS-IBTS v1.2 (2022) and BITS v1.1 (2013), both in docs_external/DATRAS_documentation/.
Survey abundance indices (CPUEA, IDX) are computed per index area defined by each expert group. The general pipeline is: construct an Age-Length Key (ALK) from CA records → derive CPUE-by-length-class from HL records → apply ALK to get CPUE-by-age → spatially aggregate with optional area weighting.
The two surveys differ mainly in their spatial stratification unit and haul validity criteria:

title: Survey Abundance Indices — Calculation Procedures
text:
1.1 General rules

Only valid hauls are used.
When ALK observations are sparse, data are borrowed from neighbouring roundfish areas (RFA); see ALK supplementation below.
For herring and sprat, only day hauls are used (based on DayNight code).
Herring in RFA 8 and 9, Q1: age ≥ 2 CPUE is set to zero (assumed spring spawners).
Two extra indices exist for Downs herring juveniles (length ≤ 12.5 cm): NS_Her1to9 (standard) and NS_Her1to7 (CPUE in RFA 8–9 set to zero).

title: Survey Abundance Indices — Calculation Procedures
text:
1.2 Calculation steps
Step I — ALK by RFA (from CA records)

Extract raw age-at-length data for species + index area.
Build ALK by roundfish area (RFA), in 1 cm classes (0.5 cm for herring/sprat).
Fill empty RFAs from neighbouring areas (see ALK supplementation).
Aggregate to plus group: ages ≥ plus group age are summed into the plus group cell.

Step II — CPUE per haul per length class (from HL records)

Apply species recording code rules; select only valid hauls.
Apply day/night filter (herring/sprat: day hauls only).
Count valid hauls per statistical rectangle.
Add zero rows for absent length classes.
Raise to total numbers: NumberAtLength × SubsamplingFactor.
Sum over SpeciesCategory and SpeciesSex.
If DataType ≠ C: NoAtHaul = count × (60 / HaulDuration) → convert to per-hour.
Sum CPUE per haul per length per statistical rectangle (per RFA).

Step III — Fill ALK for all length classes (ALKRFA)

Length class < minimum ALK length → age = 1 (Q1) or age = 0 (Q2–4).
Minimum < length class < maximum: borrow from nearest ALK entry (average if equidistant).
Length class > maximum ALK length → assign to plus group.
Merge filled ALK with CPUE by year, quarter, length class.

Step IV — CPUE at age by length class (CPUEALK)

Merge ALKRFA and CPUE by year, quarter, RFA, length class.
Sum numbers at length per age per statistical rectangle.
Sum valid hauls per statistical rectangle.
Mean CPUE at age per statistical rectangle = (2) / (3).

Step IVa — Weighted CPUE (herring, sprat, saithe only)
As step IV but hauls weighted by depth-stratum area weight of the rectangle (Annex 3 weights). Weighted mean CPUE = Σ(numbers at age) / Σ(weights of valid hauls).
Step V — Index

Sum CPUE per age over all fished rectangles in the index area.
Count number of fished rectangles in the index area.
Index = (1) / (2) → mean numbers/hour/rectangle for the index area.

title: Survey Abundance Indices — Calculation Procedures
text:
2.2 Calculation steps (6-step)
Step I — CPUE per haul per length class (HL records)

Apply species recording code rules; select valid ("V", "N") hauls and SpecVal = 1 or NULL.
Count valid hauls per SubArea (depth layer within SD).
Add zero rows for absent length classes.
Raise sub-sample to total: NumberAtLength × SubsamplingFactor.
Sum over sex and category; convert to per-hour: count × (60 / HaulDuration) (if DataType ≠ C).
Multiply by gear conversion factor (cod only) to standardise to TVL equivalent.

Step II — ALK by SD (CA records)

Compute age-length key per ICES Subdivision.
Apply plus-group rule (ages ≥ plus group age summed into plus group cell).
If ALK absent for an SD, borrow from neighbouring SDs (analogue of RFA supplementation).

Step III — Fill ALK for all length classes (same logic as NS-IBTS Step III)
Step IV — CPUE at age per depth stratum
Apply ALK to CPUE per haul × length; aggregate to CPUE at age per depth stratum (SubArea).
Step V — Weight depth strata by km²
Weight each depth stratum’s CPUE by its area in km² (see BITS_AreaWeights.csv). Area-weighted mean CPUE per SD = Σ(CPUE × km²) / Σ(km²).
Step VI — Index per index area
Sum over depth strata within each SD; then aggregate SDs into the index area mean.

NOTE: This is inferred from the data structure, so possibly wrong.
DataType R — sort, then optionally subsample: The full catch is sorted by species on deck. For low-abundance species the entire sorted pile is counted and measured (SubFactor = 1). For abundant species a random weight sub-sample is drawn from the sorted pile; only that sub-sample is measured, and SubFactor = total_sorted_weight / subsample_weight encodes the raising factor. HLNoAtLngt is the measured count in the sub-sample; TotalNo ≈ sum(HLNoAtLngt) × SubFactor recovers the estimated total catch.
DataType P — size-stratified subsampling: Same general flow as R, but the sorted catch is further divided into explicit size strata before subsampling. Each stratum gets its own CatIdentifier and SubFactor. A typical pattern is that abundant medium-sized fish are subsampled (SubFactor > 1) while rare large (or very small) fish are fully enumerated in their own CatIdentifier (SubFactor = 1) — simply because there are too few of them to bother subsampling. For example: 169 fish at 280–370 mm measured from a subsample with SubFactor 2.65 (CatIdentifier 21); 2 fish at 380–390 mm all measured with SubFactor 1 (CatIdentifier 22). The arithmetic is identical to R: n_haul = HLNoAtLngt × SubFactor, applied per stratum.
DataType S — subsample first, then sort: The bulk catch is too large to sort entirely. A random weight sub-sample is drawn from the unsorted pile; that sub-sample is then sorted and measured. SubFactor > 1 always. HLNoAtLngt is the measured count in the sub-sample; TotalNo ≈ sum(HLNoAtLngt) × SubFactor recovers the estimated total catch.
DataType C — national lab pre-raises before submission: The national laboratory has already standardised all counts to a 1-hour tow before submitting to DATRAS. The submission does not contain raw haul counts; it contains CPUE values. This does not imply that every fish was individually measured — the lab may well have applied its own sub-sampling protocol on-board — but any such raising was resolved internally and is invisible in the submitted data. SubFactor = 1 (no further raising is required by the recipient). HLNoAtLngt is fish per hour at that length, not fish in a physical sub-sample.

Four reporting modes used by national submitters:

Name
Meaning

Sorted catch; some species may be subsampled. SubFactor ≥ 1.

Sorted catch split into explicit size strata, each with its own CatIdentifier and SubFactor. Arithmetic identical to R.





NOTE: This is inferred from the data structure, so possibly wrong.
DataType R — sort, then optionally subsample: The full catch is sorted by species on deck. For low-abundance species the entire sorted pile is counted and measured (SubFactor = 1). For abundant species a random weight sub-sample is drawn from the sorted pile; only that sub-sample is measured, and SubFactor = total_sorted_weight / subsample_weight encodes the raising factor. HLNoAtLngt is the measured count in the sub-sample; TotalNo ≈ sum(HLNoAtLngt) × SubFactor recovers the estimated total catch.
DataType P — size-stratified subsampling: Same general flow as R, but the sorted catch is further divided into explicit size strata before subsampling. Each stratum gets its own CatIdentifier and SubFactor. A typical pattern is that abundant medium-sized fish are subsampled (SubFactor > 1) while rare large (or very small) fish are fully enumerated in their own CatIdentifier (SubFactor = 1) — simply because there are too few of them to bother subsampling. For example: 169 fish at 280–370 mm measured from a subsample with SubFactor 2.65 (CatIdentifier 21); 2 fish at 380–390 mm all measured with SubFactor 1 (CatIdentifier 22). The arithmetic is identical to R: n_haul = HLNoAtLngt × SubFactor, applied per stratum.
DataType S — subsample first, then sort: The bulk catch is too large to sort entirely. A random weight sub-sample is drawn from the unsorted pile; that sub-sample is then sorted and measured. SubFactor > 1 always. HLNoAtLngt is the measured count in the sub-sample; TotalNo ≈ sum(HLNoAtLngt) × SubFactor recovers the estimated total catch.
DataType C — national lab pre-raises before submission: The national laboratory has already standardised all counts to a 1-hour tow before submitting to DATRAS. The submission does not contain raw haul counts; it contains CPUE values. This does not imply that every fish was individually measured — the lab may well have applied its own sub-sampling protocol on-board — but any such raising was resolved internally and is invisible in the submitted data. SubFactor = 1 (no further raising is required by the recipient). HLNoAtLngt is fish per hour at that length, not fish in a physical sub-sample.

Distance (m) = 1.852 × 360 × (60 / 2π) ×

DATRAS implements a bootstrap approach to estimate uncertainty on abundance indices. Standard analytical variance estimators are not used because the sampling design (stratified, with ALK applied post-hoc) does not admit a simple closed-form variance.



Length distribution bootstrapping — resample hauls within each stratum (statistical rectangle for NS-IBTS; depth layer × SD for BITS) with replacement to obtain bootstrap replicates of the mean CPUE per length class.
ALK bootstrapping — resample otoliths within each age/length cell to produce bootstrap replicates of the age-length key.
Combine bootstrapped length distribution with bootstrapped ALK → bootstrap replicate of index.
Repeat a large number of times (typically ≥ 1000); compute percentile-based confidence intervals.

text: Purpose of this document. This page documents two categories of content: (1) Known Issues — problems and conventions requiring awareness or upstream correction; and (2) Quality Checks — reproducible R code to detect and verify these issues in the data.

title: DATRAS Data Issues and Quality Checks
text:
0.2 Specification Gaps
The DATRAS format specification is underspecified, inconsistent, or allows submission practices it does not formally define. Fix lies with ICES documentation and format governance.

0.2.1 Column naming convention: legacy vs. standard
Two naming conventions coexist in DATRAS, reflecting a change introduced by ICES around 2020. This is not a data quality issue per se, but a system inconsistency that causes silent failures in downstream code.








Convention
Source
Example fields




Legacy
getDATRAS() (XML API); pre-~2020 DATRAS downloads
Ship, HaulNo, StNo, LngtCode, HLNoAtLngt, SubFactor, TotalNo, HaulVal, HaulDur


Standard
Parquet files; IMBUS product; current ICES convention
Platform, HaulNumber, StationName, LengthCode, NumberAtLength, SubsamplingFactor, TotalNumber, HaulValidity, HaulDuration



Code written against one naming scheme fails silently or with cryptic errors against the other. {obus} and the IMBUS parquet use the standard names throughout.
See: D2.2 §Column naming convention



0.2.2 IMBUS interim canonical names: sex and aphia
The ICES upload schema contains naming inconsistencies that must be resolved upstream:








IMBUS name
ICES “new” name(s)
Problem




sex
SpeciesSex (HL), IndividualSex (CA)
Same concept, different names — the ICES upload field list gives the same vocabulary two different field names depending on table.


aphia
Valid_Aphia (HL, CA), AphiaID / ValidAphiaID (derived products)
Not in formal upload schema — the datacenter-resolved WoRMS identifier is named differently depending on product type.



These are interim canonical names used by IMBUS pending upstream resolution by the ICES Datacenter. Users should be aware that different systems (raw download vs. parquet vs. derived products) use different names for the same concept.
See: D2.2 §IMBUS interim canonical names



0.2.3 Cross-table semantic ambiguities
Several fields share names across tables (HH, HL, CA) but carry different meanings. Users must be aware of these semantic shifts:








Field
HL meaning
CA meaning




sex
Visual, population-level assessment (bulk catch)
Determined by dissection (individual)


NumberAtLength
Sub-sample count per length bin; multiply by SubsamplingFactor for population estimate
Count of aged fish at that length class; used as raising key for age-length keys (ALK)


LengthClass
Lower boundary of a length frequency bin
Measured length of an individual fish



Additionally, gear fields are duplicated across HH, HL, and CA with identical values — this is a submission artefact. HH is authoritative; HL and CA copies are redundant after joining.
See: D2.2 §Cross-table ambiguities



0.2.4 TotalNumber is not consistently defined across surveys
The reporting format states that TotalNumber = SubsampledNumber × SubsamplingFactor. However, empirical reconciliation reveals the two are not always equal, and the discrepancy pattern is survey-specific:
Three patterns identified:

All-sex total repeated on each sex row (Can-Mar) — TotalNumber records the total count across all sexes, but the same value is repeated on every sex-specific row. After collapsing across sexes, most Can-Mar groups reconcile.
Sex-specific TotalNumber (BTS, NL-BSAS) — TotalNumber is reported separately for each sex. Comparing against any single sex’s estimate gives apparent mismatches.
Rounding (DYFS) — TotalNumber and estimated totals both large (~2,000) but differ by ~2%, consistent with rounding during data entry.

Implication: TotalNumber should not be relied upon as a portable cross-check without knowing the survey-specific convention. The safe formula — n_haul = sum(NumberAtLength × SubsamplingFactor) from length rows — is self-consistent and does not depend on TotalNumber.
See: Quality Checks §TotalNumber reconciliation for the reconciliation check code.



0.2.5 Presence-only HL records: TotalNumber, NumberAtLength, and LengthClass all NA
Issue: Some HL records contain only a species identifier (aphia) with all quantity fields — TotalNumber, NumberAtLength, and LengthClass — submitted as NA. These are presence-only records: the submitting institute noted that a species was caught but provided no quantitative information.
Root cause: The DATRAS reporting format does not explicitly prohibit submitting an HL row with all quantity fields absent, so some institutes use this to flag incidental species presence without recording counts or lengths. This is an ambiguous submission convention — the DATRAS exchange format specification should either formally disallow it or define it as a distinct record type.
Scope (NS-IBTS 2023 Q1): 9 hauls affected (3 FR and 1 SE with DataType C; 4 NO and 1 NL with DataType R). These hauls produced 79 NA n_haul rows out of 51,924 total non-NA rows — roughly 0.15% of haul × species combinations.
In HL_standardised type == "haul" rows: Groups where all TotalNumber values are NA produce n_haul = NA. These rows are neither zeros nor valid catches — they signal a species was recorded as present but not counted. Users who filter n_haul > 0 will silently drop them.
In HL_standardised type == "length" rows (fixed): The opening filter(NumberAtLength != 0) previously dropped presence-only rows silently (SQL evaluates NULL != 0 as NULL, not TRUE), causing 72 haul × species combinations to receive spurious zero rows. Fixed in {obus}.
Recommended treatment: - Do not treat n_haul = NA rows as zero-catch entries. - For binary presence analyses, treat n_haul = NA as “detected but not quantified”. - For abundance analyses, exclude n_haul = NA rows (do not zero-fill them).

title: DATRAS Data Issues and Quality Checks
text:
0.3 Software & API Bugs
Bugs or design flaws in ICES tools (icesDatras, derived products). Fix lies in ICES software. {obus} works around both issues listed here.

0.3.1 xsi:nil column name artefact in XML API responses
Issue: When icesDatras::getCPUEAge() or icesDatras::getIndices() returns data via the XML API, columns whose values are absent or sparse arrive with xsi:nil="true" embedded in their column names:
"Age_6 xsi:nil=\"true\""
"Age_7 xsi:nil=\"true\""
...
"Age_15 xsi:nil=\"true\""
Root cause: The ICES XML API marks absent elements using the W3C XML Schema nil convention (xsi:nil="true" attribute). The icesDatras XML parser does not strip this attribute — it leaks from the XML element into the parsed R column name.
Consequence: Malformed column names cause three downstream problems:

Silent column mismatch on bind_rows() — when iterating over multiple survey/year/quarter/species combinations, some data frames may carry Age_6 (column had data) while others carry Age_6 xsi:nil="true" (column had no data). dplyr::bind_rows() treats these as distinct columns, producing a wider-than-expected table with mostly NA values in the duplicated columns.
Type coercion warnings — numeric values stored under a malformed name cannot be matched to the column type specification, triggering NAs introduced by coercion warnings even when the underlying data is valid.
Inaccessible by standard column reference — df$Age_6 or select(Age_6) will fail silently; the backtick-quoted form df$`Age_6 xsi:nil="true"` is required.

Confirmed affected record types: CPUEA (Age_6 – Age_15 in NS-IBTS), IDX (Age_7 – Age_15 in NS-IBTS), LT (e.g., Tickler xsi:nil="true"). The artefact may appear intermittently in any XML-backed record type depending on survey, year, and quarter.
{obus} workaround: The internal .strip_xsi_nil() helper is applied to every data frame before bind_rows():
.strip_xsi_nil <- function(d) {
  names(d) <- sub(' xsi:nil="true"', "", names(d), fixed = TRUE)
  d
}
See: Quality Checks §xsi:nil artefact



0.3.2 CPUEL haul key is too short for unambiguous joins
Issue: CPUEL records lack Country and StationName fields present in HH. The short key (Survey, Year, Quarter, Platform, Gear, HaulNumber) is not guaranteed unique. This creates join ambiguity when attempting to map CPUEL back to HH metadata — over 2,400 short keys are non-unique in the current data.
Root cause: A product design decision in the CPUEL output format. CPUEL computes correctly internally, but the truncated key it publishes is unreliable for downstream joins.
When joining CPUEL to HH, always use the full 8-field .id key if possible, or manually verify uniqueness for your survey/year subset. This is one of the reasons the IMBUS HL_standardised product is preferred over CPUEL.

title: DATRAS Data Issues and Quality Checks
text:
0.4 Submission Errors
Values in the submitted data that violate the DATRAS format specification. Fix lies with data providers (resubmission) or the ICES Datacenter (at-ingestion correction).

0.4.1 Size-stratified subsampling submitted as DataType R
Issue: The DATRAS schema intends DataType P for size-stratified hauls, but a minority (95 groups) are submitted as DataType R, predominantly Danish vessels in NS-IBTS and BITS from 2024 onward (82 of 95 groups). This is a submission error that should be corrected at source.
The row-level formula NumberAtLength × SubsamplingFactor remains correct, but TotalNumber reflects the stratum total, not the species-haul total.
See: D2.2 §The DataType field



0.4.2 DataType C with SubsamplingFactor ≠ 1
For DataType C, SubsamplingFactor must always equal 1. Records with missing or SubsamplingFactor ≠ 1 are submission errors and should be flagged to the ICES Datacenter.
Scope: At least 4,093+ records have invalid SubsamplingFactor values for DataType C. Combined with the ~1,856 NA values (see §SubsamplingFactor = NA), this represents a meaningful data quality issue affecting DataType C records.



0.4.3 SubsamplingFactor = NA
0.986% of valid HL records have missing SubsamplingFactor. This is a significant data submission error affecting multiple surveys and DataTypes. SubsamplingFactor is required for CPUE arithmetic and propagates as NA in computed n_haul and n_hour.
Distribution by DataType: - DataType R: 138,572 records (majority) - DataType C: 1,856 records - DataType S: 14 records
The issue spans multiple surveys, not only NS-IBTS.



0.4.4 ICES statistical rectangle boundary mismatches
StatisticalRectangle in HH should match the ICES rectangle derived from ShootLatitude/ShootLongitude. Empirically, only 0.23% of records (308 of 132,989 records with complete data, excluding Can-Mar) show mismatches. Most surveys report correct rectangles; DYFS has the highest mismatch rate (139 records).
Mismatches can indicate: - Data entry error - Boundary cases (hauls spanning rectangle boundaries; rare) - Coordinate rounding or precision issues - Minor survey-specific spatial conventions
Note: Can-Mar (Northwest Atlantic) doesn’t report StatisticalRectangle at all — it’s 100% NA. This is not a mismatch issue but a geographic exclusion (see §Can-Mar outside ICES rectangle coverage).

title: DATRAS Data Issues and Quality Checks
text:
0.5 Survey-Specific Conventions
Deliberate survey practices that differ from the general format or from other surveys. Not errors — but users must account for them.
These include the HL grouping key constancy findings: the sampling protocol fields (SpeciesValidity, SubsamplingFactor) are expected to be constant within a natural group (.id × aphia × sex × DevelopmentStage × SpeciesCategory), but several surveys have by-design exceptions.
For the StandardSpeciesCode and BycatchSpeciesCode protocol flags that govern which species are required to be recorded per haul, see Sampling protocols.

0.5.1 SpeciesValidity varies within groups (by design)
SpeciesValidity varies within 2,786 of ~2.6 million total groups (0.1%), predominantly BTS (1,289) and Can-Mar (1,272). This is intentional — full length-frequency rows (SpeciesValidity = 1) coexist with supplementary rows (totals-only, presence/absence) within the same group.
Most common co-occurrences: {1, 5} (1,281 groups) and {4, 7} (580 groups).



0.5.2 SubsamplingFactor varies within groups (size-stratified subsampling)
SubsamplingFactor varies within 389 of ~2.1 million valid groups (0.02%) due to size-stratified subsampling. Small and large fish are subsampled at different rates within the same species group.
Pattern by DataType: - P (293 groups) — all GB-SCT; the intended encoding across NS-IBTS, SCOWCGFS, SCOROC - R (95 groups) — predominantly DK from 2024 onward; submission error (should be P; see §DataType R) - C (1 group) — anomaly
Key formula: n_haul = Σ(NumberAtLength × SubsamplingFactor) applied row by row is correct for all DataTypes, including size-stratified cases.



0.5.3 TotalNumber varies by stratum (consequence of size-stratification)
TotalNumber and SpeciesCategoryWeight vary by stratum in 104 of ~2.1 million valid groups (0.005%) as a direct consequence of size-stratified subsampling. This is a data structure consequence, not an error.



0.5.4 SWC-IBTS ended 2010; superseded by SCOWCGFS
SWC-IBTS (Southwest Coast IBTS) records end in 2010 and are superseded by SCOWCGFS (Southwest Coast Continental Shelf Groundfish Survey). Account for this break when analyzing time series.



0.5.5 SWC-IBTS contains non-standard sex code “-”
Issue: SWC-IBTS contains 44,295 rows with sex = “-” (hyphen/dash). This is a non-standard sex code; the DATRAS specification defines sex as M (male), F (female), U (unsexed), or NA (not recorded).
Root cause: Unknown. The “-” code may represent: - Missing/undocumented data (equivalent to NA) - A survey-specific convention with undefined meaning - A data submission artefact
Recommended treatment: Treat sex = “-” as equivalent to NA (missing/unknown). This aligns with other surveys that report sex as NA and allows aggregation across surveys.
Scope: 44,295 rows in SWC-IBTS; no other survey exhibits this code.



0.5.6 Can-Mar uses SpeciesValidity = "5" on rows with actual length data
SpeciesValidity = "5" is defined as “presence/absence only” — the expectation is that such rows carry no length or count information (LengthClass = NA, NumberAtLength = NA). BTS follows this convention: all 9 of its {1, 5} co-occurrence rows have LengthClass = NA.
Can-Mar does not follow this convention. Of 2,805 SpeciesValidity = "5" rows in Can-Mar {1, 5} groups, 2,088 (74%) have LengthClass and NumberAtLength filled in. Inspection of 535 Can-Mar groups where both "1" and "5" rows carry length data shows:

The reason for this split is not documented in the DATRAS submission format. One possibility is that Can-Mar uses SpeciesValidity to distinguish two sampling subcategories within a haul (e.g., different gear components, sub-tows, or species-ID confidence levels). Another is that the "5" rows are a systematic submission artefact.
Practical implication: filtering to SpeciesValidity == "1" in Can-Mar discards real length data in at least 42% of affected groups. The correct treatment is unresolved and requires clarification from the Canadian data provider.

0.5.7 Can-Mar is outside ICES statistical rectangle coverage
Can-Mar (Canadian Maritime) survey does not populate the StatisticalRectangle field — all 11,372 valid Can-Mar records have NA for this field. This is correct and expected: StatisticalRectangle is an ICES grid system covering the Northeast Atlantic only (see ICES maps). Can-Mar operates in the Northwest Atlantic (Canadian waters), which falls outside the ICES rectangle system.
Can-Mar does report complete shooting coordinates (latitude/longitude at tow start) for all records (11,372/11,372) and haul coordinates for most records (6,537/11,372 = 57%). For spatial analysis, use coordinates for Can-Mar instead of relying on statistical rectangles.

Limitations in the scope of ICES-derived products. These are not bugs — they reflect the resources required to validate and produce derived products for each survey.

Derived products (CPUEL, CPUEA, IDX) are developed and verified in cooperation with ICES Expert Groups. This is time-consuming; newer surveys may lack products.

text:
1.11 xsi:nil column name artefact
Fetch a raw icesDatras::getCPUEAge() response and inspect the malformed column names directly. The example uses NS-IBTS 2022 Q1 (all species), which reliably produces the artefact on Age_6 – Age_15.

# Raw response — bypasses obus entirely
raw_cpuea <- icesDatras::getCPUEAge("NS-IBTS", 2022, 1)

# Columns carrying the xsi:nil artefact
cat("Columns affected by xsi:nil artefact:\n")
print(grep('xsi:nil', names(raw_cpuea), value = TRUE))

cat("\nColumn count:", ncol(raw_cpuea), "\n")

The artefact can cause a wider-than-expected table when bind_rows() is called across API responses with inconsistent sets of affected columns. Demonstrate by simulating two frames where one call has the artefact on Age_6 and the other does not (as would happen if the same age class had data in one survey-quarter but not another):

# Simulate the real-world mix: one frame with the artefact, one without
frame_with    <- raw_cpuea                          # Age_6 xsi:nil="true" present
frame_without <- raw_cpuea                          # same structure ...
names(frame_without) <- sub(' xsi:nil="true"', "",  # ... but artefact stripped from Age_6 only
                            names(frame_without), fixed = TRUE)
# Put the artefact back on Age_7+ to show a partial-strip scenario
for (col in grep('xsi:nil', names(frame_with), value = TRUE)[-1]) {
  names(frame_without)[names(frame_without) == sub(' xsi:nil="true"', "", col, fixed = TRUE)] <- col
}

result <- dplyr::bind_rows(frame_with, frame_without)
cat("nrow frame_with:   ", nrow(frame_with), "\n")
cat("nrow frame_without:", nrow(frame_without), "\n")
cat("ncol each frame:   ", ncol(frame_with), "\n")
cat("ncol after bind:   ", ncol(result), "  <-- extra column created\n")
cat("Duplicate Age_6 columns in result:\n")
print(grep("Age_6", names(result), value = TRUE))

Verify that the obus fix (sub() on names()) produces clean, accessible column names:

clean <- raw_cpuea
names(clean) <- sub(' xsi:nil="true"', "", names(clean), fixed = TRUE)

cat("Artefact columns remaining after fix:", sum(grepl("xsi:nil", names(clean))), "\n")
cat("Age_6 now accessible via clean$Age_6:", !is.null(clean$Age_6), "\n")
cat("head(clean$Age_6):", head(clean$Age_6), "\n")
